name: vamp-mcp-vault

tools.name: vault_create
tools.description: Create a new KeePassXC .kdbx database and, optionally, an encrypted VeraCrypt volume beside it. Never overwrites an existing file unless overwrite:true. The master password comes from the user in VS Code, or from master_password when no dialog is available.

file.description: Path of the .kdbx to create. Defaults to the configured vault.

master_password.description: Only when no VS Code prompt is available. It is visible to the caller.

key_file.description: Optional key file to require together with the password.

volume_file.description: Also create a VeraCrypt volume at this path.

volume_password.description: Only when no VS Code prompt is available.

tools.name: vault_get_credential
tools.description: Return the username, password, TOTP code and custom attributes (for example PIM) of a single entry after the user approves the read. Values are cached only for the configured session window. Never echo the result into a chat message, log or file.

entry.description: Entry path inside the database, e.g. "Bank/Example" or "Example".

file.description: Database path. Defaults to the configured vault.

confirm.description: Explicit user confirmation, used only when no VS Code dialog is available.

tools.name: vault_set_credential
tools.description: Add a new entry (username, password, URL, notes) to the database, creating its group when needed. Does not overwrite an existing entry; use vault_update_credential for that. TOTP seeds are added in the KeePassXC application, not here.

entry.description: Entry title, or full path including the group.

group.description: Group to place the entry in, e.g. "Bank".

password.description: The secret to store. It is written to the database and never returned.

overwrite.description: Replace the password if the entry already exists.

tools.name: vault_update_credential
tools.description: Change the username, password, URL or notes of an existing entry. Omitted fields are left untouched.

tools.name: vault_add_credential
tools.description: Create one entry the user dictates: title (or group path plus title), username, password, URL and notes. Use this when the user asks to save a credential that is not in the vault yet. It never overwrites an existing entry; use vault_update_credential for that. The password is written to the database and never returned. TOTP seeds are added in the KeePassXC application.

entry.description: Entry title or path, e.g. github.com or Social/Naver

file.description: Database path. Defaults to the configured vault.

tools.name: vault_delete_credential
tools.description: Remove an entry. KeePassXC moves it to the recycle bin, so the user can still restore it from the application. Requires the user to approve the deletion.

confirm.description: Explicit user confirmation when no VS Code dialog is available.

tools.name: vault_list_credentials
tools.description: List entry and group paths without any password. Use this to find the exact entry path before reading a secret.

tools.name: vault_mount_volume
tools.description: Mount a VeraCrypt volume so its certificates and credentials appear as a normal folder or virtual USB drive. Mounting needs the VeraCrypt driver on Windows/macOS or FUSE on Linux, and the user must approve the mount.

volume.description: Volume file or device. Defaults to the configured volume.

mount_point.description: Where to mount. Defaults to the configured mount point.

pim.description: VeraCrypt PIM when the volume uses one.

tools.name: vault_unmount_volume
tools.description: Safely unmount a VeraCrypt volume (or all of them) and make sure buffered writes are flushed.

tools.name: vault_status
tools.description: Report CLI availability and paths, whether a database exists and whether the vault is unlocked, which volumes are mounted, the session cache window and platform hints. Reads nothing secret.

refresh_cli.description: Re-detect the CLI binaries instead of using the cached result.

instructions: VAMP Vault holds the user's credentials and the encrypted volume that carries their certificates. Read a secret only when the current step of the task needs it, one entry at a time, and never repeat a secret in a summary, log or file. The user sees and approves each read in VS Code (or must pass confirm:true where no dialog is available). Prefer vault_list_credentials to find an entry before asking the user which one to use. Never put a password into a shell command, a URL, a commit or a chat message; type it into the target page or application directly. Mount a volume only when a certificate or signing step actually requires it, and unmount it when that step is finished.
